text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike observed in region=us-west-2 for canary model=llm-v10. p99=3.1s (baseline ~0.45s). paging oncall.

sree: oncall here, looking at dashboards. p95 ~720ms, p99 ~3.1s, streaming error rate increased from 0.7% -> 4.9%. Correlates with a deploy at 3072105940.

deploy-bot: deploy job 7890 started at 3072105900, canary ramp to 10% at 3072105940.

jamie: I see stalled streams at the streaming-router layer. Some connections deliver initial tokens then hang for 10-25s before either completing or cutting. Reproduced locally against canary traffic.

sree: timeline matches. quickest mitigation is to cut canary traffic and revert the rollout. @jamie can you set v10 weight to 0 in usw2?

jamie: executing now:
```
# rwctl cli
rwctl routing set-weight --region=usw2 --model=llm-v10 --weight=0
```
Ran at 3072105992.

jamie: watching metrics after set-weight. p99 falling but still elevated. digging into router logs.

jamie: logs show repeated KV lock contention and invalid cache keys for v10 sessions. sample:
```
2026-03-15T10:46:12Z router WARN kv_cache mismatch session=usr-42 model=llm-v10 token_prefix=\u0000
2026-03-15T10:46:12Z runtime INFO kv_write backend=rocksdb key=session-usr-42 size=64
2026-03-15T10:46:13Z router WARN streaming stall session=usr-42 reason=kv_lock_wait
```
Hypothesis: v10 tokenizer produced different token id ordering which changes key derivation for KV prefix -> cache thrash -> lock waits -> head-of-line streaming stalls.

sree: that explains p99 tail. Under multiplexing we amplify impact since many virtual sessions await the lock. For immediate relief, recommend: (1) revert traffic (done), (2) disable multiplexing for v10 routing, (3) throttle KV writer rate.

jamie: applying mitigations:
```
rwctl routing set-multiplex --region=usw2 --model=llm-v10 --enabled=false
rwctl kvctl set-throttle --region=usw2 --backend=canary-kv --rate=120/s
```
Applied at 3072106018.

sree: after mitigations p99 down to ~620ms, p95 ~520ms, streaming error rate back near baseline. Good.

ellen (Support): Support log: ~15 distinct customer sessions showed truncated/incomplete assistant responses between 10:42-10:58 PDT. Examples: AcmeCorp (3 sessions), BetaFinance (2 sessions). Symptoms: "partial response, then connection cut" and clients re-sent with duplicate tokens.

mike (CS): AcmeCorp flagged this morning, we've opened a contact thread. ETA for customer note: 10m.

dina (PM): high level RCA hypothesis? infra bug, model artifact, or tokenizer issue?

jamie: quick triage points to tokenizer/KV key incompatibility in the canary build. v10 introduced a tokenizer optimization that changed token id mapping for rare tokens. Our KV key includes token prefix -> mismatch.

sree: agreed. create an incident ticket and assign owners. Proposed severity: Sev3 (partial degradation, limited customers). Ticket RINF-INC-2026 created.

jamie: coding plan: add compatibility shim to canonicalize token prefixes before KV keying, add unit tests for token->key mapping. Ticket for runtime+ml infra: RINF-4391. ETA for server-side shim (fast path) ~6-8 hours; full test-backed fix ~48 hours.

ellen (Support): contacting affected customers now. CS outreach list: AcmeCorp, BetaFinance, GammaApps. Draft message: "We observed intermittent streaming interruptions between 10:42-10:58 PDT after a canary deploy. We reverted the canary and applied mitigations. We're investigating root cause and will provide ETA for fix." Sending in 8.

mike (CS): AcmeCorp asked for a phone call if ETA slips. Logged their request.

sree: handoff plan: I'll monitor for 15m to confirm stability, then hand to ops-rotation for postmortem and customer comms. Please attach logs & dashboards to the incident ticket.

jamie: also note: we aborted the canary promotion job 7890 at 3072106035.

deploy-bot: job 7890 aborted at 3072106035.

sree: monitoring window complete. metrics stable for 20m. handing to @ops-rotation. handoff timestamp 3072106205.

ops-rotation: acknowledged, taking ownership for postmortem coordination and customer follow-ups. Will schedule PM and owner sync.

dina: decisions: (1) do not re-promote v10 until fix validated (2) communicate proactively to affected accounts (3) prioritize the tokenization compatibility fix in next sprint.

jamie: implementation notes: we'll add a canonical token-key translation layer in routing to ensure backward-compatible KV keys. We'll also add integration tests that run tokenizer variants against key computation.

ellen (Support): actions logged: outreach complete for critical accounts, incident note in CRM, attach logs to RINF-INC-2026, schedule postmortem.

mike (CS): sent AcmeCorp update with current status and ETA options (hotfix vs full fix). They acknowledged and will wait for follow-up.

ops-rotation: creating postmortem draft, assigning jamie + runtime infra as authors. Incident moved to incidents backlog with follow-ups: RINF-4391 (bug), RINF-INC-2026 (incident).

deploy-bot: incident marked closed (in monitoring) at 3072106405. follow-ups remain.

sree: final summary for record: root-cause hypothesis = tokenizer id/order change in llm-v10 -> KV key mismatch -> cache thrash & locking -> streaming stalls -> p99 spikes. Live mitigations = revert canary, disable multiplex, KV throttle. Next steps = implement compatibility shim, tests, and run a constrained canary after validation. Handed to ops-rotation for postmortem & customer comms.
